audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Azariah/Uzziah, northern coups, Tiphsah atrocity, Assyrian tribute and deportation, and Jotham narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for adolescent accession, chronic skin disease and separate residence, delegated governance, repeated assassinations, Tiphsah massacre including pregnant women, imperial tribute extracted from wealthy people, palace coup, Tiglath-pileser deportations, and escalating Aram-Israel pressure on Judah.

verses.restored: In twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
Sixteen years old was he when he became king, and fifty-two years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in eyes of YHWH, according to all Amaziah his father had done.
Only high places were not removed; people were still sacrificing and burning incense at high places.
YHWH struck king, and he had a skin disease until day of his death and lived in a separate house. Jotham king's son was over house, judging people of land.
Remaining acts of Azariah and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
Azariah lay with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in city of David. Jotham his son became king in his place.
In thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH as his fathers had done; he did not turn from sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him before people, put him to death, and became king in his place.
Remaining acts of Zechariah, look, they are written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel.
This was word of YHWH spoken to Jehu, saying, Sons of fourth generation shall sit for you on throne of Israel. And it was so.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah and reigned one full month in Samaria.
Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, came to Samaria, struck Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, put him to death, and became king in his place.
Remaining acts of Shallum and his conspiracy that he made, look, they are written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel.
Then Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territory from Tirzah. Because it did not open to him, he struck it and ripped open all its pregnant women.
In thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel and reigned ten years in Samaria.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH; all his days he did not turn from sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
Pul king of Assyria came against land, and Menahem gave Pul one thousand talents of silver so his hand would be with him to strengthen kingdom in his hand.
Menahem brought out silver from Israel, from all mighty men of wealth, fifty shekels of silver from each man, to give to king of Assyria. King of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in land.
Remaining acts of Menahem and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel?
Menahem lay with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son became king in his place.
In fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned two years.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH; he did not turn from sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him in Samaria, in citadel of king's house, with Argob and Arieh and fifty men from Gilead. He put him to death and became king in his place.
Remaining acts of Pekahiah and all he did, look, they are written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel.
In fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned twenty years.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH; he did not turn from sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
In days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, all land of Naphtali, and exiled them to Assyria.
Hoshea son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him, put him to death, and became king in his place, in twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
Remaining acts of Pekah and all he did, look, they are written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel.
In second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah became king.
Twenty-five years old was he when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in eyes of YHWH; according to all Uzziah his father had done, he did.
Only high places were not removed; people were still sacrificing and burning incense at high places. He built upper gate of house of YHWH.
Remaining acts of Jotham and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
In those days YHWH began to send against Judah Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah.
Jotham lay with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in city of David his father. Ahaz his son became king in his place.

translation_notes: The Hebrew term for Azariah's condition is tsara'at, a broad ritual/skin-disease category, not an automatic diagnosis of Hansen's disease. Translation must avoid the stigmatizing blanket term 'leper.'

Azariah lives separately while Jotham governs. Disability or chronic illness does not erase personhood, moral agency, family bonds, or political identity, and isolation should not be romanticized as proper care.
The northern throne passes through repeated public and palace assassinations. Brief reigns and coup success are not evidence of legitimacy.
Menahem's attack on Tiphsah and ripping open pregnant women are war crimes and reproductive violence. They must be named without graphic sensationalism or ethnic generalization.
Pregnant people and unborn children are not symbols in a royal contest; their bodies expose the extremity of state terror against a city that resisted entry.
Menahem taxes wealthy Israelites to buy Assyrian support for his throne. The payment may prevent occupation temporarily while turning public wealth into regime security.

Assyrian deportation removes entire communities from Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and Naphtali. Exile is coercive population transfer, not a clean geopolitical change.
The chapter's regnal synchronisms are complex and require historical-textual audit; apparent arithmetic tensions should not be silently harmonized.
Mothers' names remain part of Judah's royal record and should not be treated as blame markers for sons' actions.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize skin disease or disability, glorify coups, sanitize the Tiphsah atrocity, blame victims of reproductive violence, or treat deportation as ordinary administration. Center bodily dignity, pregnant people's humanity, civilian protection, and the cost of using taxation and empire to secure a throne.
